question: Which platform has the best soft skills training for employees, like communication and emotional intelligence?
text:
If you're choosing a platform for employee soft-skills training, rather than just an individual course, my top pick would be LinkedIn Learning.

My ranking
Platform	Best for	Communication	Emotional intelligence	Enterprise/L&D
LinkedIn Learning	Best overall	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Coursera for Business	Deeper, structured learning	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Udemy Business	Huge breadth & flexibility	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐
Specialist providers	High-impact behavior change	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐
🥇 Best overall: LinkedIn Learning

I'd choose it if you want employees to actually use the training library regularly, rather than complete one long course.

LinkedIn Learning currently has dedicated learning paths for professional soft skills, including emotional intelligence, communication, teamwork, critical thinking and resilience. Its business-communication certificate covers interpersonal communication, conflict and communicating with confidence. 
L
LinkedIn
+1

There's also a Human Skills for Managers path covering emotional intelligence, communication, motivating employees and leading through change. 
L
LinkedIn

LinkedIn Learning for Business

Why I'd pick it: excellent combination of short, approachable content + breadth + enterprise administration.

🥈 Best for deeper learning: Coursera for Business

I'd pick Coursera if you want employees to go beyond "watch a 30-minute video" and actually build a more structured skill set.

For example, Coursera has courses covering emotional intelligence, active listening, empathy, conflict management, communication and leadership, with assessments and shareable certificates. 
C
Coursera
+1

Its current soft-skills catalog also includes IBM's People & Soft Skills: Essential for Professional Success, which covers collaboration, presentations, constructive feedback, communication and teamwork. 
C
Coursera

Coursera for Business

🥉 Best for sheer content variety: Udemy Business

I'd consider Udemy if your employees have very different development needs and you want an enormous range of courses.

It's particularly good when you want employees to choose courses themselves, although I'd be more selective about curating a company-wide curriculum because quality can vary between instructors.

My recommendation by use case

"We need a good soft-skills library for the whole company." → LinkedIn Learning

"We want serious development programs with assessments/certificates." → Coursera for Business

"We want maximum choice and lots of niche topics." → Udemy Business

"We specifically want to transform communication/EQ behavior, especially for managers." → I'd look beyond generic course libraries at a specialist behavioral-skills provider.

One important distinction: the best platform isn't necessarily the provider with the best courses. For communication and emotional intelligence, I'd prioritize platforms that include practice, scenarios, reflection, feedback and manager reinforcement. Watching 40 videos about empathy rarely changes workplace behavior on its own.
